I just got done at the store shopping for my fuel for an ultramarathon this weekend. I picked up my normal fuels, fruit gummies, snickers, cliff bars, and chocolate donettes, but I went to a different store and picked up a few unique items to this store. One of them is this awesome apple/date based bar much like a larabar, but a lot cheaper. As I was doing my shopping I basically just wanted to buy 6000 calories worth of food that I knew I could eat while running. I burn about 600 calories an hour, but I also know I usually lose my appetite while running and have to force myself to eat so this seems like enough food to fuel me if I need it, and it won't be a ton extra if I run a little light on fuel a couple of times.

Anyway, as I was shopping I really wasn't looking at anything except the total caloric content of the package and if it was something I would find tasty enough to be able to eat on the trail. I added up each of my boxes and when I hit right around 6000 calories I grabbed a case of gatorade and walked to the register. It occurred to me that this is why I'm able to successfully manage my weight. I treat food as a fuel and not entertainment or comfort. If I need 6000 calories of food, I go buy 6000 calories of food. I don't go up and down every single aisle looking for a bunch of things I don't need. If I'm not working my butt off I don't eat high calorie cliff bars. If I'm about to do a short easy run, I have a couple hundred calorie snack. I never ever reward myself for burning 1000 calories by eating 2000 calories. It's fuel not a reward.

Anyway, I never really thought about this before but it's clearly the exact opposite of how overweight people view food and I dare say if they could figure this one little thing out they might actually lose some weight.
